clue.text: Proposition from her to me, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of these three words may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone passes a suggestion from one person to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange the letters of HER TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a statement in logic or mathematics put forward for proof, which is what a proposition is.

clue.text: Disease, one caught by birds given scraps

indicators.note: something caught by the birds is held inside their word

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
TB is tuberculosis
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sick birds are given leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' signals the container; the disease and the numeral sit together inside the birds, not after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Titbits are small tasty pieces of food, like scraps fed to birds.

clue.text: Throe and ache alternate reciprocally

indicators.note: alternate is read as a different arrangement of the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Pain and spasm take turns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternate' rearranges THROE and ACHE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things to each other means doing them mutually, which is what reciprocally means.

clue.text: Woman's holding court over here, causing strain

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the letters are turned upwards, read from bottom to top
holding means one piece contains another

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's courtroom ordeal causes her stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' builds the container first, then 'over here' turns the whole thing to read upwards, as a down clue allows.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain to vomit.

clue.text: Sources of pleasing aromas — US smokers, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: American cigarette smokers give off nice scents, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges US SMOKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The musk rose is a climbing rose valued for its strong sweet scent.

clue.text: Book is written on biological inheritance

indicators.note: something written on another item comes after it in an across entry, so the word is follows

parts.note: genes carry what living things inherit from their parents

explanation.surface: A text about heredity, the sort of book a biologist reads.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis is the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: to buckle in wind

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'to buckle in wind (5)' is cut short: GA(B)LE needs a word giving B before 'to buckle', and the definition is missing.

clue.text: Crossly turn on people tucking into Italian food

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece on top of the next
crossly read as in a crossed, jumbled way, so the letters of turn are mixed
tucking into means going inside another piece

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: An angry diner rounds on others eating Italian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossly' scrambles the first word only; 'on' stacks that above the rest in a down clue, and 'tucking into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutriment is nourishment, anything that feeds the body.

clue.text: Divine wisdom

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to perceive by intuition

explanation.surface: Holy insight.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to divine it, and good sense is practical wisdom.

clue.text: Staff at the Palace

parts.note: reads as royal servants but means a ceremonial rod held by a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's ornamental rod, carried as a symbol of royal power.

clue.text: The ounce possibly to make a comeback it's understood

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back the other way, so the feline word is read backwards

parts.note: the ounce is a snow leopard, so an example of a big cat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rare snow leopard returning to the wild is taken as read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make a comeback' turns CAT into TAC; 'it's' gives IT plus a link 'is'. The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, not the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied without being stated, so it is silently understood.

clue.text: Wealth and position associated with work in journalism?

parts.note: a sub, or sub-editor, checks and trims copy on a newspaper
a stance is a position taken on an issue

explanation.surface: A journalist's money and standing tied to their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associated with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of substance is rich, so substance can mean wealth or means.

clue.text: Old American finally captured by Irish cavalry 28 must be loco

indicators.note: something captured by others is held inside them, so these letters go into the Irish cavalry pieces

parts.note: cavalry are soldiers on horse, so horse can stand for them

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word American

explanation.surface: An elderly American taken prisoner by Irish horsemen must be crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured by' signals the container round O and the last letter of 'American'. 'loco' looks like American slang for mad, but it is short for locomotive. The '28' is a stray print mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron horse was an old nickname for a steam locomotive, and loco is the usual short form.

clue.text: Sluggish gold-digger initially wasted time

indicators.note: the first letter is lost, wasted away from the front of the word

parts.note: a gold-digger is literally a miner digging for gold

explanation.surface: A lazy fortune-hunter squandered the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold-digger' suggests a mercenary partner, but here it is a literal digger for gold; 'initially wasted' drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert describes something without energy or motion, as sluggish does.

clue.text: Asian gentleman ploughed his BA

indicators.note: ploughed means turned over like soil, so these five letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman in India failed his degree.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'ploughed' is old British student slang for failing an exam, which is the surface; as the indicator it turns HIS BA over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was the respectful title for a man, especially a European, in colonial India.

clue.text: That's life

parts.note: sounds like a shrug of resignation but describes a written account of someone's life

explanation.definitionFit: A book telling the story of a person's life story is exactly what this genre is.

clue.text: Fellow loses bishop-end of game

indicators.note: loses says one letter is dropped from the companion word

parts.note: a stablemate is a fellow member of the same stable or group
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: In chess, a player gives up a bishop and the game ends in deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' removes the B from STABLEMATE. The chess setting is apt: a stalemate ends a game of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalemate is a chess position with no legal move, so the game finishes drawn.

clue.text: Country once wrongly initially

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Country once wrongly initially (9)' is garbled: no wordplay for ABYSSINIA can be built from these words, so part of the clue is missing.

clue.text: Answer phone call, having phoned in putting in order

indicators.note: in places the past-tense word inside the call word

parts.note: a ring is a telephone call
rang means phoned

explanation.surface: Someone takes a call and then rings back to sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals that the past tense goes inside the call word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging things means setting them out in a planned order.

clue.text: Before end of May sun lover's looking out anxiously

indicators.note: Before puts the rearranged phrase ahead of the final letter
looking out of sorts, so the letters of the phrase are disordered

parts.note: the possessive s adds no letter

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word May

explanation.surface: A sunbather peers out with worry before summer arrives properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking out' scrambles the sun-lover phrase; 'end of May' adds a final Y, and 'Before' sets the anagram ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something nervously means doing it with worry or unease, as anxiously does.

clue.text: Pet scheme revealed by son in bridge contract, just falling short

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for son inside the bridge bid
falling short means the last letter is missing

parts.note: no trump is a bridge contract played without a trump suit

explanation.surface: A favourite plan is exposed by a son at the bridge table, narrowly failing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just falling short' cuts the P from NO TRUMP, and 'in' puts S inside. 'revealed by' joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a pet remedy or favourite scheme for solving a problem.

clue.text: Sound of machinery, with rumble being partly eliminated

indicators.note: partly says only part of the run of letters across these two words is used

explanation.surface: Engines hum on, their rumble only half quietened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes the letters inside 'wiTH RUMble'; 'being eliminated' is surface padding read as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a steady low humming noise, such as an engine makes.

clue.text: Go after this expensive property?

parts.note: reads as urging someone to chase a costly house, but on a British Monopoly board the Go square follows the dearest property

explanation.walkthrough: In the British edition of Monopoly the most expensive square is the last before Go. It is also a costly district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The priciest site on the British Monopoly board, and a wealthy area of London's West End.

clue.text: As always article escapes cut

indicators.note: an article escaping means the letter leaves the phrase

parts.note: as ever means as always
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: As usual, a newspaper piece avoids the editor's scissors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escapes' drops the first A from AS EVER to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut through or cut off.

clue.text: Minister, one about to be received by queen

indicators.note: received means taken in, so these pieces go inside the royal letters

parts.note: VR stands for Victoria Regina, Queen Victoria
I is the Roman numeral one
ca is short for circa, meaning about

explanation.surface: A clergyman receives an audience with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: VR, Victoria Regina, is a standard crossword queen; 'to be received by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, a minister of the church.

clue.text: My legitimate desire

parts.note: something just is lawful or fair
a fancy is a liking or desire

explanation.surface: Someone claims their wish is perfectly reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks like a possessive but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, as in 'My, you have grown!'

clue.text: Gives someone time to pay his debts?

definitions.text: Gives someone time to pay his debts?

parts.words: Gives someone time to pay his debts?
parts.note: reads as allowing a debtor longer to settle, but means sentencing him to time behind bars as payment

explanation.definitionFit: Locking up offenders, once the fate of debtors, is giving them time in prison.

clue.text: Expression of disgust about child's brief appearance in piece of film

indicators.note: about says the exclamation goes around the other piece

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust
CH is a short form of child

explanation.surface: A grimace at a child's cameo in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the exclamation wraps around the short form of child.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiche is a flat sheet of microfilm.

clue.text: Class of infants having a party

definitions.meaning: in British primary schools the first class, for four- and five-year-olds, has this name
a formal gathering to welcome guests, as after a wedding

explanation.surface: The youngest pupils at school are having a party.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the first infant class carries this name, and a formal welcoming party is also called one.

clue.text: Popular tea found thereabouts?

indicators.note: thereabouts means round about, so the word for tea goes around the other piece

parts.note: cha is a British colloquial word for tea
in means popular, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: Where does a well-liked brew come from?
explanation.walkthrough: 'thereabouts' signals the container. The whole clue is the definition as well, since China is where much popular tea is grown.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a country famous for growing and drinking tea.

clue.text: Female's title assumed by aesthetic types commemorated in Oxford?

indicators.note: a title assumed by someone is taken on, so it goes around the other piece here

parts.note: Mrs is a title for a married woman
arty means having artistic or aesthetic pretensions

explanation.surface: A woman takes a married name among a group of artistic folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumed by' signals the container. The Martyrs' Memorial in Oxford commemorates three Protestant bishops burnt there in the 1550s.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford's Martyrs' Memorial honours churchmen who died for their faith.

clue.text: One evening

parts.note: read not as a time of day but as one who is evening things up, settling a score

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes revenge squares accounts, getting even with a wrongdoer.
